property_summary: A PROPOSER_ROLE holder can schedule an operation only with delay >= getMinDelay(), in which case getTimestamp equals block.timestamp + delay; scheduling with an insufficient delay reverts and leaves no operation pending.
Granting the EXECUTOR_ROLE to an account from the TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE holder makes hasRole return true, and granting again leaves it true without reverting.
An account granted the TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE has that role immediately, and any caller without it cannot grant roles (grantRole by a non-admin reverts).
A PROPOSER_ROLE holder can cancel a pending scheduled operation, after which the operation is no longer pending and its timestamp is zero.
Scheduling an operation with delay >= minDelay sets its timestamp to block.timestamp + delay, while scheduling with an insufficient delay reverts and leaves no operation.

property_summary: Only the timelock contract itself can change the minimum delay: updateDelay always reverts when called by anyone else, leaving getMinDelay unchanged.
The deployer holds TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, so grantRole from the deployer succeeds and makes hasRole(role, account) true for any role and account.
After the admin grants and then revokes a role, the account no longer holds it.
A scheduled pending operation can be cancelled by a proposer, after which its timestamp is zero and it is no longer an operation.
After a proposer schedules an operation with sufficient delay, cancelling it removes the operation so that its timestamp becomes zero and it is no longer an operation.
After a proposer schedules an operation with delay >= minDelay, the operation's timestamp equals block.timestamp + delay, making it pending but not ready or done.
grantRole for a role whose admin is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE reverts when called by an account without that admin role, and leaves the role unassigned.
updateDelay always reverts when called by an account other than the timelock contract itself, and the minimum delay remains unchanged.
A schedule call by a proposer with a delay below the minimum delay reverts and does not create the operation.
Scheduling an operation with delay >= the current minimum delay records its ready timestamp as exactly block.timestamp + delay, and cancelling it resets that timestamp to zero.
After scheduling an operation with a delay at least the minimum delay, its recorded timestamp equals block.timestamp + delay.
Scheduling reverts unless the caller holds the PROPOSER_ROLE.
updateDelay always reverts when called by any account other than the timelock contract itself.
hashOperation returns exactly keccak256(abi.encode(target, value, data, predecessor, salt)) for all inputs.
